articles.title: Valve will start selling the Steam Deck on February 25th
articles.summary: After a delay, Valve’s handheld gaming PC is almost here. The Steam Deck will go on sale starting February 25th, as those with reservations will get emails to complete their orders and start receiving the devices as soon as the 28th.
articles.body: Valve announced that the Steam Deck will go on sale starting February 25th. According to the company’s blog, customers who have reservations will get an email on that day and have three days to place an order. Valve also says that it’ll release new batches on a weekly basis, so if you’ve got a reservation, March will be the time to keep an eye on your email. Here’s some more info from Valve’s announcement: > We will start sending invites shortly after 10:00 am on February 25th, PST Order emails are sent in the same order that reservations were made. You can only order the Steam Deck model that you originally reserved. Your reservation deposit will be applied to the final price of Steam Deck, and shipping costs are included. The release date matches Valve’s recent prediction that the console would start heading out to gamers by the end of February. Valve says that the orders placed on the 25th will start shipping out on the 28th. [Media: It’s good to finally have a date for when the handheld console will be coming out. When Valve announced the Steam Deck in July 2021, it was originally slated to ship in December of that year. However, it was delayed by two months due to the supply chain and shortage issues that have become standard with many product launches. Valve is still letting you reserve the Steam Deck for $5 if you haven’t already. You could have quite a wait at this point, though — the order page currently says that you can expect to order “after Q2 2022.” If you’re still on the fence, you can check out our hands-on impressions of the Steam Deck here, and watch the video below. [Video: Steam Deck: a Switch-like portable gaming PC]

articles.title: How to Navigate the Brandon Sanderson Cosmere Series Timeline
articles.summary: Where should you start?
articles.body:
If you consider yourself a fan of high fantasy, I would be willing to bet that there is a good chance you have at least heard the name "Brandon Sanderson" even if you have never read one of his books. Widely considered one of the most prolific fantasy authors of the modern age, Sanderson is a titan of the industry, having redefined publishing for authors, fought for better contracts for author e-book sales, brought about the conclusion of the legendary Wheel of Time series after the passing of its original author, Robert Jordan, and has basically created his own media empire with Dragonsteel (complete with his own convention). To say that he is a big deal would be underselling it a bit.

All that aside, perhaps what Brandon is best known for is the Cosmere—his universe-spanning interconnected monolith that a majority of his various books and series take place somewhere in. Picture the Marvel Cinematic Universe but as books, and all by the same writer. When a new Cosmere book is released, it's a big deal. This list will give you a basic idea of the (current) chronological order of the books in the scheme of the Cosmere itself, omitting books that we know are coming (Dragonsteel, the future Elantris Books, Mistborn eras 3 and 4, etc) but have not yet been released. With the news of Brandon Sanderson's Cosmere universe getting picked up by Apple TV , there's never been a better time to dive into the series.

If you look at the long list of titles that currently take place in the Cosmere, it can feel like a Herculean task to get through some of the books on their own, so consider this more as a resource to help you navigate it a bit, and make connections along the way as you read through the various series. However, just be aware that these can also be enjoyed on their own as smaller self-contained series, without needing to read them in chronological order. Special thank you to the CopperMind (a Cosmere resource kept up to date by the most diehard of fans) for helping me put this list together. Just be careful when you go on there as it is really easy to accidentally spoil things for yourself (speaking from experience, even though they try to mark everything).

It should be noted that as of this writing, there is no official timeline, with Brandon having previously stated that he hopes to have one released before the second Arc of Stormlight Archive releases—tentatively planned for 2031 (no, I'm not joking). The current list was put together thanks to research and input from the Coppermind wiki, Reddit, and YouTube videos

How Many Books Exist in the Cosmere Timeline?

As it stands right now, if you want to read everything the Cosmere has to offer, you will have to work your way through a pile of graphic novels, short stories, novelas, and your standard novels. All told, you are looking at about 25 books to buy (the number gets a little wonky depending on how you count the books that count the collections of stories and such), but here is a list of all the Cosmere titles you will need to read:

Mistborn Era 1 Mistborn: The Final Empire The Well of Ascension The Hero of Ages

Mistborn Era 2: The Alloy of Law Shadows of Self The Bands of Mourning The Lost Metal

Stormlight Archive 1st Arc The Way of Kings Words of Radiance Oathbringer Rhythm of War Wind and Truth

White Sand (Graphic Novels) White Sand Vol. 1 White Sand Vol. 2 White Sand Vol. 3

Arcanum Unbounded (Collection of Short Stories and Novellas) The Emperor’s Soul The Hope of Elantris (free on Brandon Sanderson’s website) The Eleventh Metal Allomancer Jak and the Pits of Eltania Mistborn: Secret History White Sand Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell Sixth of the Dusk Edgedancer

The Hope of Elantris (free on Brandon Sanderson’s website)

Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

The “Chronological” Cosmere Reading Order

While the following breakdown will take you through the Cosmere as we believe it to exist right now, it isn’t necessarily the “best” way to tackle these books. There are a number of options that people recommend, reading in Publication Order is a common one, knowing how imposing this all is, Brandon released his own “Where do I start?” list that you can check out too. I started with Mistborn Era 1 (Mistborn: The Final Empire) and then into Stormlight Archive Book 1, and had a good time.

Believed to be set first chronologically, the White Sand graphic novels take place on Taldain , a desert world where individuals can be trained to become Sand Masters. Following a man named Kenton who is training to be one, the three volumes focus on him trying to get to the bottom of who was behind a surprise attack that killed many of the other Sand Masters. White Sand ran from 2016 to 2019 and is based on a manuscript that was one of Brandon’s earliest works, with an excerpt of this early writing included in the Arcanum Unbounded collection. You can expect that occasional easter egg or nod to White Sand in future books, but not as much as other entries (yet) in the Cosmere.

Elantris: Tenth Anniversary Author's Definitive Edition

Taking place on the world of Sel , Elantris was Sanderson's first published work , released back in 2005. Due to various factors in later books, it is assumed that Elantris takes place very early in the timeline of the Cosmere books. The story follows a few different viewpoints, including the crown prince Raoden, of a kingdom known as Arelon, his soon-to-be bride Princess Sarene, and the high priest Hrathen. The namesake of the book, 'Elantris' is the name of a city that, years before the book, a cataclysm known as the Reod robbed the Elantrians of their almost god-like powers and magic, and left them as to what could only be described as sentient zombie-like people.

Elantris plays around with the idea of what happens when a world's magic system simply breaks, and no one knows how to fix it. It is a fun read with its fair share of surprises and twists. While we know that Sanderson is planning two sequels for Elantris, as of 2025, this remains a stand-alone novel, but not the only one set in the world of Sel.

The Hope of Elantris (Arcanum Unbounded)

The Hope of Elantris takes place during the events found at the end of Elantris with an aim to fill in some gaps and moments in the story, providing further context. As such, this absolutely should not be read before finishing Elantris; instead, enjoyed as a little extra dessert afterwards. To further sweeten the deal, in addition to being included in the Arcanum Unbounded collection, you can actually read this completely for free off of Sanderson’s website!

Taking place on Sel, after the events of Elantris and The Hope of Elantris, but in a different nation, The Emperor’s Soul follows a thief named Shai, who has been tasked with recreating the soul of an Emperor. This book introduces new magic that had previously not been seen in the other Sel set books, and offers a more asian-inspired setting and theme. It’s a fun read, and getting a grasp on this new magical forgery trick will come in handy as you read future books. This is one of the novellas included in the Arcanum Unbounded collection.

Mistborn Era 1 (Vin and Kelsier) - World: Scadrial

Mistborn: Secret History (Arcanum Unbounded - READ AFTER HERO OF AGES)

The Mistborn titles , especially the first Era, are some of the most well-known and beloved of the Cosmere-connected books, and a wonderful first stop if you want to expose yourself to Sanderson's writing and style. Taking place in the world of Scadrial , era 1 focuses on the adventures and exploits of a young thief named Vin, and Kelsier, a legend in his own time, as they work to overthrow the current empire and create a new world order.

Some people of this world are able to "burn" or use a variety of metals they swallow for different effects, like pushing off of metal, altering the emotions of nearby people, and more. In the scope of the Cosmere, the events that transpire on Scardrial will prove immensely important to future books, and are a must-read for anyone to really get into this universe. There's even a Mistborn board game for fans of the series looking to head to the tabletop.

Mistborn: Secret History (Arcanum Unbounded)

Mistborn: Secret History is a tough one to discuss, as nearly everything about it will be rather spoilery. This novella takes place between the events at the end of The Final Empire and the start of Hero of Ages. Read this after finishing Mistborn Era 1, and don’t look up anything about it until then unless you want big spoilers!

The Eleventh Metal novella serves as a prequel to the original Mistborn: The Final Empire book. It explores Kelsier's early days after receiving his allomantic abilities, as he learns from his teacher, Gemmel. This short story was initially included in the Mistborn Adventure Game, but was later included in the release of Arcanum Unbounded. While chronologically speaking, this is before the main Era 1 books, you will get more out of it, reading it after you have finished at minimum The Final Empire, if not Hero of Ages.

The exact placement of Warbreaker is still a bit up for discussion, whether it takes place before Mistborn era 1 or after, but we do know for certain that it is before the Stormlight Archive. Taking place on the world of Nalthis , Warbreaker focuses on the two princesses, Vivenna and her younger sister Siri. Circumstances throw both of the sisters into situations they weren’t prepared for, Siri needing to take over in a role that was to be handled by her sister, and Vivenna needing to find a new purpose in life while also doing what she can to save her sister. Should they succeed, it may just prevent a war and prevent an invasion of their home..

As it currently stands, much like Elantris, Warbreaker is a standalone book, but Sanderson has promised a follow-up to Warbreaker sometime in the future. Warbreaker and some characters within do have a larger impact on the Cosmere and other worlds, making this a pretty important book to read, but luckily, it isn’t incredibly long, having been published relatively early in his career back in 2009. Warbreaker also has the added benefit of introducing arguably the best sentient sword in all of fantasy with Nightblood.

Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell (Arcanum Unbound) - World: Threnody

At roughly 18,000 words, Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell is a short novella that you can bust out in a sitting or two. Taking place in the world of Threnody , currently believed to be only a minor planet in the Cosmere’s story as a whole (so far), Shadows follows Silence Montane, the proprietress of a waystop in the Forests of Hell. She accepts a bounty to track down a notorious highwayman, and things quickly get rocky for Silence, which will have repercussions for her family. Inside the Arcanum Unbounded collection, Sanderson also includes a small essay that elaborates a bit more on the Threnodite system in the Cosmere. This story is a nice little palate cleanser to read between larger works.

The Stormlight Archive Arc 1 - World: Roshar

Edgedancer (Book 2.5 - Arcanum Unbounded & Standalone )

The Stormlight Archive is Brandon Sanderson's behemoth of a series , with books often spanning more than 1100 pages.. Taking place on the planet of Roshar , Stormlight Archive immediately immerses readers into the middle of a long-standing conflict between the Alethi (a kingdom of Humans) and the Parshendi, a humanoid people adorned with a carapace that grows from them. The conflict began years earlier after the assassination of the Alethi king.

This series defines the genre of "epic fantasy" more so than any other of Sanderon's work, with readers being treated to an intricate magic system, a staggering amount of lore and world building, and wonderful cast of characters that you will follow as you try to piece together what has lead to the events in these books, and what is to come. From magic knights to gods, heroes forced to rise to the occasion and a world where emotions are given shape in the form of creatures known as 'Spren', this first arc of the Stormlight Archive finds itself smack dab in the middle of the Cosmere, both chronologically speaking and as a central pillar of the universe itself.

The final book of this first part of the Archive, Wind and Truth, was released in December 2024. The next book is not expected until sometime in the early 2030s , so luckily, there is still plenty of time to dive in and get caught up. This is a must-read to get into the Cosmere, but not one that I would recommend as a jumping-in point. This entire arc takes place over the course of about two years.

Taking place between Books 2 (Words of Radiance) and 3 (Oathbringer) of the first act of the Stormlight Archive, Edgedancer follows the character of Lift, who is first introduced in an interlude in Words of Radiance. This young thief has a decidedly unique tone and personality when compared to others on Roshar, and this novella would be best enjoyed after completing Oathbringer.

Dawnshard takes place between Oathbringer and Rhythm of War, the third and fourth books of the Stormlight Archive, and follows Rysn and other notable Stormlight characters, including the beloved “The Lopen”. Moments from this book are mentioned in Rhythm of War, so you will be fine reading it beforehand, but it is just as enjoyable reading it after, to get a better handle on events mentioned in the book. Also, you get more Lopen, which is never a bad thing.

Misborn Era 2 (Wax and Wayne) - World: Scardrial

Wax and Wayne, The Mistborn Saga Boxed Set

The second era of the Mistborn titles picks up about 300 years after the events of The Hero of Ages on Scadrial. Whereas the first set of books took place in a more medieval society, the world of Scadrial now resembles something more akin to the American Frontier or the early Industrial Revolution. The second era follows the exploits of the mercenary allomancer lawman, Wax, and his partner Wayne, dealing with the newer threats posed by the advances of technology and also the problems caused by the events that transpired in the past. This all results in a set of stories that feels both familiar and brand new all at the same time, with some of the most beloved characters in the Cosmere.

It’s advised that you don’t tackle the Wax and Wayne books until you have completed at least the first set of Mistborn books. However, as being one of the more recent Cosmere releases, the fourth and final book, The Lost Metal, starts working in more connections with the Cosmere as a whole, so you will get more out of that last book especially, the more of the previous books of the Cosmere you have read already.

Sixth of the Dusk (Arcanum Unbounded) - World: First of the Sun

Among the entries contained within Arcanum Unbounded, Sixth of the Dusk takes place the furthest down the timeline. Set around the large island known as Patji on the planet known as First of the Sun , this short novella (clocking in just under 18,000 words) follows a trapper named Sixth of the Dusk as he tries to save his home. This book is currently believed to take place rather far ahead in the timeline of the Cosmere as it features a race of people with advanced space travel technology. It also has magic parrots.

Tress was the first of Brandon Sanderon’s Secret Project Kickstarter titles that he wrote during the pandemic, unbeknownst to anyone but his wife. A standalone novel taking place in the world of Lumar , which is home to an emerald green ocean of spores, Tress of the Emerald Sea is about a young girl who sets out to find and rescue her love. Sanderson describes his inspiration for Tress as “what if Buttercup from the Princess Bride had been more proactive.”

Currently, Tress of the Emerald Sea is believed to be somewhere in the distant future of the Cosmere, but where it precisely lands is a mystery.

Taking place on the world of Canticle , where the sunlight can melt the very stone, The Sunlit Man was the fourth book of Brandon’s Secret Projects and follows the immortal known as Nomad , who is caught in a conflict between rebels and a tyrant. Much like the other secret project novels, this is also a standalone title that takes place far in the future of the Cosmere, but its specific placement is nebulous.

Even though this is a standalone title, it’s recommended that you don’t read this until you finish the first arc of the Stormlight Archive because…reasons…

Yumi and the Nightmare Painter - World: Komashi

Yumi and the Nightmare Painter, third of the Secret Projects, takes place on Komashi , where mysticism and technology butt heads against one another. Following the characters of Painter, who works as a Nightmare Painter (someone that captures dark beings) and Yumi (a traveling priestess that can summon and command spirits). A string of events binds the two of them together, and they have to figure out why and how to get out of it.

Yumi and the Nightmare painter is standalone and feels decidedly different from other books in the Cosmere, with its setting being a mix of Japanese and Korean influences, with Brandon mentioning that the initial concept came from his exposure to the manga Hikaru no Go and other media like the anime film Your Name and Final Fantasy X. Believed to take place far in the future of the Cosmere, this can be a fun first outing to dip your toes into the Cosmere.

The Fires of December: A Cosmere Novel (Hoid's Travails)

The Fires of December is another standalone fantasy novel in The Cosmere, serving as another part of Hoid's Travails. Taking place aon a minor planet called Miral that is sustained by colorful rivers of demon blood, the story follows and orphan named December as she discovers a cataclysmic plague.

This book is available now, and was also part of the Hoid's Storybook Collection crowdfunding campaign that launched this year. You can check out IGN's hands-on experience with the premium hardcover to see what that looks like.

Stormlight Handbook, Cosmere RPG Core Rulebook

Brandon Sanderson, in collaboration with Brotherwise games, has officially released the first set of Cosmere RPG books. Here's a quick snippet of what I thought in my full Cosmere RPG review :

"The Cosmere RPG is putting a strong foot forward right out of the gate, with systems that manage to feel familiar while at the same time doing its own thing that sets it apart. I appreciate its more flexible character growth and heavier emphasis on your own personal story and incorporating it into tangible gameplay features. It remains to be seen just how well the team manages to balance and intermingle the vastly different worlds and magic systems that inhabit the Cosmere. Still, I am already chomping at the bit for the next world guides, handbooks, and what Brotherwise Games have up their sleeves."

What We know Is Coming in 2026 and Beyond

Much like our own universe, the Cosmere continues to expand. Back in December of 2024, Brandon gave his updated PLANNED release schedule up through 2031 , and is as follows:

December 8, 2026: The Fires of December (out now as an eBook)

December 2026: Dark One or Isaac’s Cosmere Novel

November 2027: War for Roshar Board Game ( The Kickstarter is now live )

December 2028: Mistborn Era 3 - Book 1 (Ghostbloods)

December 2031: Stormlight Archive Book 6 (begins 2nd Arc)

Brandon Sanderson and Apple TV have officially solidified a deal to bring The Cosmere to the screen. There are no official release dates just yet, but reports have confirmed that Mistborn is being eyed for feature films and The Stormlight Archive is likely to become a TV series. Sanderson took to the Comsere Reddit after the announcements to tell the fans more about the deal, saying he chose Apple TV due to "the level of approvals and control" as well as their track record for high quality content.

The most recent progress update from Brandon Sanderson revealed he's officially done with the Mistborn screenplay and is awaiting feedback. However, during an IGN interview Sanderson said the adaptations is still 'many years off', suggesting a release date of 2031 or later .

Sanderson also revealed that he has started workin on Ghostblood revisions again. He also recently got his other YA series Skyward picked up for an adaptation as well, which is receiving a new book series in September 2026.

Scott White is a freelance contributor to IGN, assisting with book and tabletop game coverage. Follow him on X/Twitter or Bluesky .

articles.title: Peak Has Been Leaked for PS5 by the ESRB
articles.summary: The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak, has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB.
articles.body:
The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak , has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB.

Last year, an adorable, cheap co-op game known as Peak blew up on Steam . In the game, players unite with their friends to pass through a wide variety of deadly obstacles in order to climb absurdly tall mountains. They must use the power of friendship and a handful of tools to overcome the odds, often resulting in hilarious deaths, injuries, and hijinks. As of August 2025, Peak has sold over 10 million copies , partially thanks to the fact it only costs $8 and is an easy sell to a group of friends.

It seems like the game will likely only continue to grow its audience, as the ESRB has rated Peak for PS5. Historically, ESRB leaks are incredibly accurate, so it seems like only a matter of time before an official announcement is made. As of right now, it's unclear if Peak will also come to Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2, but it would be surprising if this remained console exclusive to PS5.

Unfortunately for new players, Peak ended its post-launch support earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't expect the game to receive any significant content after it releases on console. It's also unclear if it will enjoy the same exceptionally low price when it does hit consoles, but it would be surprising if the team behind the game changed it. Following the game's release, the team noted that there's a psychology behind pricing a game that low .

“We had this joke of, like, 'How much is a game really?'" said Peak co-creator Nick Kaman. "In a player’s mind, what does it mean to spend five bucks? Well, that’s five bucks. But six bucks? Well, that’s still five bucks. Four bucks is also kind of five bucks. Three bucks is two bucks. And two bucks is basically free. So we’ve got these tiers: You know, twelve bucks… that’s ten bucks. But thirteen bucks is fifteen bucks. And we found that eight bucks is still five bucks. It doesn’t become ten bucks. Seven ninety nine, that’s five bucks, right? So, eight bucks going to five bucks is the biggest differential we could find in pricing, so we found it very optimal.”

It's unclear when an official announcement might follow, but if there's an ESRB rating, it typically means that the game isn't too far away from a release.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Fanttik Has a Great Deal on an All-in-One Electric Air Duster and Power Bank
articles.summary: For a limited time, you can pick up the Fanttik B10 Pro Max Electric Air Duster and Power Bank for $44.99 with free shipping after you apply this coupon code.
articles.body:
Fanttik has a pretty cool accessory that covers both maintenance and energy recharge in one compact device. For a limited time, you can pick up the Fanttik B10 Pro Max Electric Air Duster and Power Bank for $44.99 with free shipping after you apply coupon code " IGNB10PM ". You don't need to be an Amazon Prime member to take advantage of this deal.

Fanttik B10 Pro Max Electric Air Duster and Power Bank in One

Fanttik B10 Pro Max Electric Air Duster and Power Bank

The Fanttik B10 Pro Max is first and foremost an electric air duster. This palm-sized device features a 130,000 RPM brushless fan that pushes air at a velocity of 65m/s with a "megaboost" button for an extra surge of airflow. There are six levels of intensity, and the highest level is more than enough power to clear out the dust from your PC or the grime from your keyboard. Four different nozzles are included, including one that allows you to fill air up in inflatables.

Two 4,000mAh batteries (8,000mAh total) allows you to use the air duster cordlessly, and therein lies its second use an 8,000mAh power bank. You don't want to use this as your main battery backup for your electronics, since it's bulkier than your typical power bank and the USB-C port only has a maximum output of 10W. However, it's quite useful in a pinch, and I'm not sure why other electric air dusters don't have this functionality since nearly all of them run off lithium batteries. The USB-C connectivity means it is natively compatible with most devices, including your iPhone 18 or Nintendo Switch.

articles.title: Why Rays have all the momentum heading into Game 3 of ALCS vs. Guardians
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays entered Tuesday facing the possibility of falling behind 2-0 in the American League Championship Series. Instead, their 3-1 victory over t...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays entered Tuesday facing the possibility of falling behind 2-0 in the American League Championship Series. Instead, their 3-1 victory over the Cleveland Guardians at Tropicana Field restored their confidence and shifted the pressure before Thursday's Game 3 in Cleveland.

Freddy Peralta provided the biggest reason for optimism. The right-hander tossed six scoreless innings, allowing four hits and two walks while striking out six. He also reached 99.4 mph, the fastest pitch of his major league career. Acquired from the New York Mets in August, Peralta delivered exactly the kind of postseason performance the Rays desperately needed.

His outing also gave Tampa Bay a blueprint for attacking Cleveland's lineup throughout the series. By limiting scoring opportunities and preventing the Guardians from building early momentum, Peralta allowed the Rays to play from ahead. That formula becomes increasingly important as the series moves to Progressive Field, where Cleveland will have the crowd behind them.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The bullpen reinforced that advantage. Kevin Kelly, Ian Seymour and Bryan Baker combined to finish the victory. Although Chase DeLauter hit a run-scoring double in the seventh, Seymour escaped further damage and Baker worked a perfect ninth for his fourth save of the postseason.

The Rays' offense also demonstrated how its aggressive base-running can pressure opposing defenses. In the fourth inning, Victor Mesa Jr. advanced to third on Chandler Simpson's infield single when Jose Ramirez failed to cover the bag. Ramirez then misplayed Ben Williamson's grounder with two outs, allowing the Rays to plate their first run of the evening. Liam Hicks followed with a two-run single, extending the lead to 3-0. All three runs charged to Parker Messick were unearned, highlighting Tampa Bay's ability to capitalize on Cleveland's defensive mistakes .

That opportunistic approach matters against a Guardians team that won four consecutive playoff games before Tuesday. Cleveland scored seven runs in a Game 1 win, but Tampa Bay held its lineup to one in Game 2, interrupting the surge that had carried the Guardians through the Division Series.

The Rays also have evidence that their approach has worked vs. Cleveland. They took five of six regular-season meetings, outscoring the Guardians 20-8. Their 98-win season and three-game ALDS sweep of the New York Yankees further demonstrate their strength.

The Guardians will host Games 3, 4 and, if necessary, 5 at Progressive Field, giving them an opportunity to regain control of the series. However, the Rays avoided a potentially devastating 2-0 deficit and now head to Cleveland with renewed confidence. Their dominant pitching, aggressive base-running and ability to capitalize on mistakes could prove decisive as Tampa Bay looks to take control of the ALCS.

articles.title: Surprised Rays SP Freddy Peralta reacts to Steve Cohen’s presence at ALCS Game 2
articles.summary: Freddy Peralta must be thanking his lucky stars that the Tampa Bay Rays managed to acquire him at the trade deadline. After all, not only was he struggling p...
articles.body:
Freddy Peralta must be thanking his lucky stars that the Tampa Bay Rays managed to acquire him at the trade deadline. After all, not only was he struggling personally to the tune of a 4.99 ERA with the New York Mets, the Mets were also in the middle of a disastrous 2026 campaign. Instead of watching the postseason from the couch, Peralta now has the opportunity to play a huge role in the Rays' quest to win the franchise's first World Series title.

Peralta proceeded to show out on Tuesday as he pitched six shutout innings to power the Rays to a 3-1 victory over the Cleveland Guardians to even up the ALCS at 1-1. He has not allowed more than one earned run in each of his past eight starts, and he seems to be rediscovering his best self, as he even reached 99.4 mph on his fastball in Game 2 of the ALCS.

One surprise fan in attendance in Tropicana Field on Tuesday was Mets owner Steve Cohen , Peralta's former employer. At the very least, the 30-year-old cleared up that he and Cohen have a good working relationship .

"Oh, I had no idea. You know, I don't even know what to say because I don't know if he came just to watch the game or maybe me too. What I can say is that we have a good relationship. When he traded for me, he texted me, we spoke," Peralta said in his postgame presser, via Foul Territory on X.

articles.title: Rays Even ALCS Against Guardians as Freddy Peralta Delivers Dominant Game 2 Start
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in Game 2 of the ALCS to even the series 1-1. Freddy Peralta delivered six scoreless innings with six str...
articles.body:
In a game they absolutely needed, the Tampa Bay Rays evened the series, taking down the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in Game 2 of the American League Championship Series at Tropicana Field.

Tampa Bay's pitching stepped up, and the offense did just enough to bring the series to one game apiece before hitting the road for Cleveland later in the week.

Here is what you need to know for the contest.

It was a fantastic night for the Tampa Bay pitching staff led by Freddy Peralta. The American League Pitcher of the Month for September continued to show his dominance on the mound with six shutout innings and striking out six Cleveland Guardians in the process.

By doing so, Peralta becomes only the second pitcher in Rays history to throw a scoreless quality start this deep into the postseason, joining Scott Kazmir, who did the same in Game 5 of the 2008 ALCS.

Peralta continues to show his dominance and remind folks what a great trade deadline Erik Neander had for Tampa Bay.

The rest of the bullpen stepped up as Kevin Cash utilized some familiar faces to finish this one off, as Kevin Kelly, Ian Seymour, and Bryan Baker all pitched stellar performances. Kelly was the only one to allow an earned run across 17 pitches, when Chase DeLauter picked up an RBI double.

It wasn't a perfect night for the Tampa Bay batting order, but it was enough, especially with elite pitching to complement it. Tampa Bay picked up seven hits and, unlike Game 1, didn't send one out of the park for a home run.

All the runs came in the bottom of the fourth inning, following a Jose Ramirez error that was quickly taken advantage of by Liam Hicks on a first-pitch 2-RBI single.

The bottom of the lineup for Tampa Bay was more efficient, as four of the seven hits came from the last four places in the order.

Tampa Bay will now need to win on the road if they want to take advantage of the ALCS, as the next two games will be at Progressive Field, the home of the Cleveland Guardians. Griffin Jax will get the start for Game 3, pushing Nick Martinez to Game 4. He is scheduled to face Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams. First pitch on Thursday is scheduled for 6 pm Eastern.

articles.title: Ubisoft Cuts 70 Staff From Skull and Bones Dev, Shuts Down Trials Studio RedLynx
articles.summary: The cuts and studio shutdowns continue at Ubisoft, this time with layoffs hitting the developer of Skull and Bones and the closure of Trials maker RedLynx.
articles.body:
The cuts and studio shutdowns continue at Ubisoft, this time with layoffs hitting the developer of Skull and Bones and the closure of Trials maker RedLynx.

GamesIndustry.biz reported that Finnish studio RedLynx will close down, with up to 52 people losing their jobs. Meanwhile, Ubisoft Singapore, developer of pirate game Skull and Bones , will lose 70 staff. In a statement, Ubisoft insisted Ubisoft Singapore “remains an important part of Ubisoft’s global production organization.” GI said 70 staff represented around a fifth of Singapore’s total headcount, which suggests 280 staff are left.

Skull & Bones suffered a notoriously choppy development that stretched out over years. After a series of delays, it eventually launched early 2024 with a $70 price tag that Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot justified by describing Skull & Bones as a "quadruple-A game." Year 3 Season 2, titled Crimson Waters, launched in August.

RedLynx, meanwhile, was gobbled up by Ubisoft in 2011 having enjoyed enormous success with the likes of Trials 2 , Trials HD , and Trials Evolution , games that challenged players to navigate increasingly difficult side-scrolling courses on a bike. But after the launch of Trials Rising in 2019, RedLynx became a Ubisoft support studio.

It’s a sad end for RedLynx, once one of the most high-profile Xbox Live Arcade developers in the business. I have many fond memories of playing Trials HD and Trials Evolution on lunch breaks with colleagues at my previous stomping ground, Eurogamer, where we’d laugh and shout our way to the finish line in local competitive multiplayer. Trials was Infuriating — of course it was, it’s called Trials — but so much fun.

Ubisoft is of course still cutting costs left, right, and center across the business as it reorganizes itself into a leaner operation focused on fewer games. Multiple studios have closed down in recent years, many staff have lost their jobs, and games have been canceled.

Most recently, Natalie Francis was appointed Studio MD of Massive Entertainment, with Thomas Andrén’s becoming General Manager for Ubisoft’s Creative Network. Massive Entertainment, based in Malmö, Sweden, is currently leading the development of The Division 2 and The Division 3, operates development on the Snowdrop game engine, and works on Ubisoft Connect.

Modern Warfare 4 (full game including Multiplayer) officially launches on October 23 across all platforms, but you’ll be able to play the campaign a week before that with Early Access, which kicks off on October 16. DMZ, Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode, is available from October 20.

All Multiplayer Maps in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 global release times:

As I said above, Modern Warfare 4 officially comes out on October 23, but what time you’ll get access depends on whether you have Early Access and what platform you plan to play on.

Modern Warfare 4 players on PC will be able to jump on at midnight local time on the morning of October 23. Wherever you’re based, the game will unlock at midnight. If it doesn’t trigger straight away, fully close and exit Steam — a relaunch should trigger it.

When does Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Early Access start?

Campaign Early Access for Modern Warfare 4 begins on October 16, 2026, for players who digitally preorder the Standard Digital Edition or Vault Edition of the game. For people who bought physical, there’s no Early Access for preorders of the Standard Edition.

When does Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Access start?

Additionally, players who preordered will get Early Access to DMZ mode, which kicks off on October 20.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developer Rockstar Insists Its Next Game Won't Take Another 8 Years to Make
articles.summary: Rockstar has promised that its next game following GTA 6 won’t take as long to come out, although it failed to hint at what it might be.
articles.body:
Rockstar has promised that its next game following GTA 6 won’t take as long to come out, although it failed to hint at what it might be.

GTA 6 finally launches in November, eight years after the release of its last game, Red Dead Redemption 2. In a new report by Bloomberg detailing the challenges Rockstar has faced during GTA 6’s development, company leadership said whatever’s next won’t take as long because the work done for GTA 6 provides a foundation for following it up faster.

“The engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly,” Phil Hooker, co-head of development, said.

“I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content.”

“We foundationally changed a lot of stuff on this project,” co-head of development Aaron Garbut added. “But now it’s done, and we’re not going to rip it apart.”

The question fans have is, what will Rockstar’s next game be? Bloomberg compares the release of GTA 6 to GTA 3, in that the first 3D GTA game paved the way for the quickfire release of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which launched a year later in 2002. Could Rockstar soon follow GTA 6 with another GTA game, perhaps focused on another city?

Many hope and expect Rockstar to make Red Dead Redemption 3, although Rockstar itself hasn’t indicated it has plans to do so. A year ago, Rockstar Games co-founder and former lead writer Dan Houser said RDR3 “will probably happen.” In 2023, Roger Clark, who played Arthur Morgan, the main playable protagonist of Red Dead Redemption 2, said he was “certain” fans would see Red Dead Redemption 3 “one day,” but qualified that statement by saying he had no idea when that would be. Clark also ruled out the return of Arthur Morgan in the game, should it come to be. If you’ve played Red Dead Redemption 2, this might seem like stating the obvious, but there’s always the chance Rockstar may consider another prequel of some kind.

“I’m certain we will see Red Redemption 3 one day,” Clark said. “When that will be — I have absolutely no idea. Don’t count on Arthur’s involvement either. His story has been told, I feel.”

In a subsequent interview with IGN , Clark expanded on his thoughts: “Yeah, that got really picked up! I would have thought that was obvious though. Wouldn’t you? And it’s not like I have any insider information whatsoever, but of course there’s going to be another Red Dead. It sold over 60 million copies!”

He continued: “Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Take-Two said it himself. He said GTA and Red Dead are prominent franchises for Rockstar Games and that they will be returning to them in the future. So there’s no doubt there will be another Red Dead. But if Arthur Morgan will be involved? I highly doubt it, to be honest. And I think it’s going to be quite some time before we even see a snifter of anything new Red Dead related. I have no idea how it would pan out, but I wouldn’t bet on Arthur being a part of it.”

In April this year, Hollywood star Jack Black revealed the character he’d love to play in Red Dead Redemption 3 , should Rockstar make the game: Jack Black. In lieu of a Red Dead Redemption movie, which Black said he’d very much love to star in if the opportunity ever came his way, the Bowser actor would love to star in Red Dead Redemption 3. And it turns out there’s a character called Jack Black he’d love to play.

"Red Dead Redemption 2 takes place around the turn of the century, right?" Black told Polygon while promoting The Super Mario Galaxy Movie . "There was a character around that time named Jack Black, who wrote an autobiography called You Can't Win. I would kinda like to play Jack Black in Red Dead Redemption 3."

articles.title: Battlefield 6 Skins With Way Too Many Pistols and Spelling Errors Spark AI Accusations
articles.summary: Battlefield 6 has come under fire from fans after its latest battle pass was found to include new character skins with some pretty clear design flaws.
articles.body:
Battlefield 6 has come under fire from fans after its latest battle pass was found to include new character skins with some pretty clear design flaws.

The first that stands out is the soldier wearing some kind of Batman mask, but minus the ears. He has five pistols attached to the chest pockets of his tac vest, for when you positively, absolutely have to go Shiva mode on some clowns. “Because switching to your pistol, secondary pistol, tertiary pistol, quartenary (sic) pistol, and quinary pistol is faster than reloading, soldier!” one Reddit poster joked .

💀 BRO IS CARRYING 5 PISTOLS! WHO APPROVED THIS SKIN? 😭 #Battlefield6 — Battlefield Intel (@BattlefieldInte) October 13, 2026

💀 BRO IS CARRYING 5 PISTOLS! WHO APPROVED THIS SKIN? 😭 #Battlefield6

Illogical pistol placement isn’t the only thing weirding fans out. Some are convinced some of the skins were actually created with generative AI, after noticing weird spelling errors and other inconsistencies. One of the skins has a patch that says “secuty” on it, which is presumably supposed to say “security.”

Secuty 😭 It's AI #Battlefield6 — Battlefield Intel (@BattlefieldInte) October 13, 2026

"I believe it’s almost impossible to deny anymore that EA/DICE is using AI for the skins in #Battlefield6,” said one X / Twitter poster . “At least in the concept phase — and then anything that looks even remotely 'cool' just gets rubber-stamped.”

Another skin features a bomb disposal juggernaut with thick body armor and a completely exposed head, like a cheeky little turtle poking out of its shell. Imagine aura farming when the shrapnel starts flying. It doesn’t help that he’s carrying magazines for small game hunting rifles that don’t exist in Battlefield 6.

“Fps .22s probably take like 2 full mags to kill someone,” one X / Twitter user said . “Not to mention he's carrying super finicky mags for a .22 varmint rifle,” joked another .

The Year Ahead for Battlefield 6 | 2026 Roadmap - Screenshots

While it's possible that these skin issues are the result of human error, fans aren't giving DICE the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps that shouldn't come as much of a surprise; AI is perhaps the hottest topic in the video game industry, and with the likes of Fortnite developer Epic Games going all-in on generative AI , there is an intense scrutiny and a healthy dose of skepticism around video game assets that contain clear errors, particularly when they cost money to buy.

Elsewhere, fans are feeling misled over the inclusion of more whacky cosmetics. As well as a reactive weapon skin , there are crossover cosmetics with other EA series, allowing Battlefield 6 players to do some Dead Space cosplay. These land ahead of the Battlefield 6 Dead Space event .

It’s not quite Nicki Minaj, but the inclusion of these skins goes back on what the developers said prior to launch. Developers at DICE had gone on the record to say Battlefield 6 won’t feature goofy, immersion breaking skins .

articles.title: Rockstar Pushes Back on Rumor GTA 6 Cost More Than $1.5 Billion to Make, but It's Still Probably the Most Expensive Video Game of All Time
articles.summary: Rockstar has insisted GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make, countering an online rumor, but it’s still probably the most expensive video game of all time.
articles.body:
Rockstar has insisted GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make, countering an online rumor, but it’s still probably the most expensive video game of all time.

In a sweeping report by Bloomberg into the making of GTA 6, Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe insisted a rumor that GTA 6’s budget was more than the $1.5 billion spent on Dubai’s Burj Khalifa was wrong, although she failed to confirm the game’s exact budget. This rumor appears to have emerged from a July 2025 article by Gulf News , which claimed “Dubai's landmark is said to have cost $1.5 billion but the game is thought to have a $2 billion budget.”

Earlier this year, Business Insider suggested a $1-1.5 billion budget based on industry analyst estimations as part of an interview with Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two. Zelnick wouldn’t say how much the company had spent on GTA 6 so far, but did admit “it was expensive.”

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

While GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to develop, according to Rockstar, it is considered the most expensive video game of all time. The only video game that might claim to come close to GTA 6’s budget is space sim Star Citizen, although its now over $1 billion budget comes from ongoing sales of space ships. Bungie's recently released extraction shooter reportedly had a budget of over $250 million , for example. Concord's initial development deal was around $200 million, according to a report by Kotaku . In 2023, documents submitted as part of the Xbox Federal Trade Commission case accidentally revealed The Last of Us: Part II and Horizon Forbidden West each cost more than $200 million to develop . Last year, the astronomical development budgets of the Call of Duty games were revealed for the first time after a court document confirmed Activision pumped $700 million into Black Ops Cold War alone, although that was over the shooter's life cycle. GTA 6, clearly, surpasses them all.

As part of Bloomberg’s report is the confirmation that Rockstar now has 4,711 staff across 12 offices, up from the 2,441 staff it had when Red Dead Redemption 2 came out in 2018. The company has doubled in size over the last eight years, which will have increased costs significantly.

As Bloomberg points out, GTA 6’s enormous budget is likely to pay off pretty quickly, with some predicting an eye-watering 40 million sales and $3 billion in revenue in the first four months of the game going on sale in November. The standard edition of GTA 6 costs $80 — a $10 hike on the standard price of a triple-A video game. The Ultimate Edition, which some consider to be an essential purchase, costs $100. Then there’s the expected launch of online multiplayer next year (maybe tied to the launch of the PC version, which is reportedly due out Q1 2027 ), which will surely boost revenue even further. In short, even if it’s just shy of $1.5 billion, GTA 6’s budget doesn’t feel like much of a risk.

In July, Newzoo analysis suggested GTA 6 generated approximately $180 million in digital preorders across the U.S. and the five biggest European markets during the last week of June (GTA 6 preorders went live at midnight, June 25). The analytics firm used GTA 5’s player distribution (around 69% of GTA 5's lifetime console players sit within those six markets) to then estimate global first-week preorder spending for GTA 6 at approximately $260 million. Based on comparable preorder curves, GTA 6 is currently tracking toward $3.25 billion to $5.2 billion in cumulative sales by the end of launch week, it said.

GTA 5 set records for generating $1 billion in three days after going on sale back in 2013, making it the fastest-selling entertainment product in history (Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Endgame ran it close, making $1 billion at the global box office in five days). GTA 6 seems certain to hit the $1 billion mark faster than both. GTA 5 went on to become the second best-selling video game of all time, with nearly 230 million units sold-in to date. Only Minecraft is ahead of it. Could GTA 6 eventually surpass even Minecraft's 400 million sales?

In other GTA 6 news, Bloomberg reported that Rockstar has promised its next game won’t take another eight years to develop , although we don’t know what it will be.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: The New Sense and Sensibility Movie Is a Plain Jane Adaptation of a Classic Romance
articles.summary: Sense and Sensibility review: A plain Jane adaptation of a classic romance.
articles.body:
Sense and Sensibility is in theaters on October 16.

Georgia Oakley’s Sense and Sensibility is one of the most eye-catching films you’re likely to see this year, but as an adaption of Jane Austen’s first novel — which she published anonymously; its authorship was originally “By A Lady” — it feels, ironically, cinematically anonymous. There’s an awkwardness to its unfolding, thanks in large part to how it engages with the novel’s tone — or rather, how it fails to — resulting in a film that barely splits the difference between social farce and genuine romance. It’s certainly watchable, but when it comes to such esteemed material, is that enough?

Sticking closely to its source, the late eighteenth century plot follows the plight of the Dashwood family — primarily sisters Elinor (Daisy Edgar-Jones) and Marianne (Esmé Creed-Miles) — when their patriarch dies, leaving them with little and forcing them to vacate their lush estate. Along with their mother, Mrs. Dashwood (Caitríona Balfe), and younger sister Margaret (Bodhi Rae Breathnach), the girls soon relocate to a more humble abode. Elinor and Marianne then become respectively smitten with eligible bachelors amid the complications of procedure surrounding marriage, engagement, and inheritance in Georgian England.

These societal confines determine the movie’s dramatic contours as the headstrong Elinor reminisces about her summer spent with the dashing Edward Ferrars (George Mackay), and the more sprightly Marianne becomes acquainted — by way of a classic, bumbling meet-cute — with the roguish John Willoughby (Frank Dillane) while rejecting the advances of the too-uptight Colonel Brandon (Herbert Nordrum). As questions about the sisters’ financial compatibilities clash with the men’s white lies and half-truths, things gradually fall apart.

A key problem with the film’s unspooling emerges early on as the Dashwoods lament their lack of riches moving forward, courtesy of a selfish half-brother, the cartoonishly scheming John Dashwood (Tom Brooke), and his equally sinister wife, Fanny (Stacy Martin). For most movies, a picturesque setting backed by melodic, dreamlike strings would be an unequivocal strength, but in this version of Sense and Sensibility, the movie’s inviting aesthetics fit jaggedly alongside its borderline satirical tone, which doesn’t end up solidifying.

There are occasional jokes and exaggerations played completely straight amidst painterly visual compositions, resulting in a clumsy dissonance that leaves this iteration halfway between class satire and captivating drama. Arnaud Potier’s 35mm photography results in gorgeous natural surroundings and a sense of vivid visual contrast, but the behavior it actually captures is a tad malformed. A key element of the novel — and of previous adaptations like Ang Lee’s 1995 Oscar winner starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet — is a bubbliness underscored by a complicated sisterly dynamic. While Edgar-Jones and Creed-Miles seem to play younger, more age-appropriate versions of the Dashwoods, their personalities are reliant on exposition to explain who each of them is and why they’re apparently so different.

The filmmaking rarely emphasizes elements of their personalities; it’s a failing that becomes especially apparent during an attempt at a comedic beat when a minor supporting character, Lady Middleton (Chloe Pirrie), discusses the weather. It’s a gag meant to highlight how boring she is, but very few of the characters around her have much more life or energy to them themselves. There are certainly standouts who deliver alluring, energetic performances, from Fiona Shaw as the talkative, kindly aunt Mrs. Jennings to the Dashwoods’ larger-than-life neighbor, Sir John Middleton (Turlough Convery), but they also overshadow the leads by several degrees despite their attempts to inject the sisters’ dynamic with life and mischief.

Oakley’s filmmaking creates a distinct sense of place and time, but the movie’s emotional moods are often at the mercy of humdrum drama lacking in judicious close-ups and other shot selections to shake things up a bit. These stilted scenes by and large play out at an unobtrusive distance of lukewarm medium shots; the camera is never close enough to conjure real emotions or removed enough to highlight the era’s class absurdities.

It’s an adaptation stuck in the middle, unable to decide between contemporary commentary on outdated social mores or full-tilt absorption into the era’s drama. Are these women justifiably aggrieved or silly for caring too much about status? You can certainly decide for yourself, but the movie’s lens doesn’t seem to gesture at one conclusion or the other despite both possibilities lingering in the ether, making it hard to be fully invested either way.

articles.title: Deathstroke Star Joe Manganiello Speaks Out About Ben Affleck's Canceled Batman Movie
articles.summary: Deathstroke actor Joe Manganiello has opened up about the impact the cancellation of Ben Affleck’s Batman movie had on him.
articles.body:
Deathstroke actor Joe Manganiello has opened up about the impact the cancellation of Ben Affleck’s Batman movie had on him.

Magnaliello, who popped up as Deathstroke brielfy at the end of Zack Snyder's Justice League, was set to reprise the role in as the lead antagonist in a standalone Batman film. Manganiello was battling an autoimmune disease at the time, which saw his weight drop from 235 to 176 pounds. Deathstroke, he said, was his reason to push forward and get back to full health.

“I just knew I needed to fight. I needed to get in better shape, I needed to gain the weight back that I had lost in the hospital,” he told Entertainment Weekly . The movie was reportedly ambitious, planning to tie together 80 years of Batman mythos .

11 Batman Villains Who Deserve Great Movies

As well as starring alongside Manganiello as the Caped Crusader himself, Ben Affleck was originally down to write and direct the Batman movie before stepping down as director. The film was eventually canned, with Snyder's DCEU falling by the wayside with the release of Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom in 2023. These changes meant Manganiello’s appearance as Deathstroke was also doomed.

"I lost my mind when that happened,” Manganiello said of Batman's cancellation. “It was so tough. Because I took me being offered that role as the villain of Batman as the universe saying it’s gonna be okay. And when it went away, I didn’t have that to fight for anymore. And it was almost like, I now looked in the mirror, and for the first time since getting sick and having surgery, I saw the scars and I realized this didn’t happen to someone else — this happened to you.

“At the time I saw it as being unlucky. What I came to understand through the full journey was that I was lucky to get it. It was never meant to be for me. It was there to make sure I didn’t stop fighting, and that I was in the best shape possible for when they tried to reconnect my digestive system.”

While Manganiello has come to terms with the loss of the role and recovered from his health issues, there’s still a part of Deathstroke he can’t let go of. “You know, I have that helmet from when I got to play him for the first time sitting in my office and I look at it every day, and it’s the greatest achievement of my life,” Manganiello said when asked if he’d still be up for playing the character. “I’ve been to hell and back. You want a warrior? You know who to call.”

Affleck himself recently discussed the collapse of his Batman movie , telling the Happy Sad Confused podcast that the experience of working on Justice League turned him off to the idea of having to helm a movie in the DC universe.

"The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons," Affleck said. "Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You're really making a mistake. That was what really doomed that."

Filming is currently underway for The Batman Part 2 , which sees Robert Pattinson and Matt Reeves team up to continue the story of a young Batman figuring out where his moral line is. While filming had been underway for a few months, The Batman Part 2 recently halted filming as the director stepped away for personal reasons. It’s planned for an early 2028 release.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Releases New Gameplay Video Showing Snippets of the Final Missions, Declares 'The End of the Road' After Crypto Scheme Collapses
articles.summary: Cyberleek has released a new GTA 6 gameplay video showing snippets of the ending, and declared "the end of the road" after their crypto scheme collapsed.
articles.body:
The GTA 6 leaker has allegedly released a new unauthorized gameplay video which reportedly shows parts of the ending of the story, sparking significant spoiler concern among fans online. IGN will not report on the details of the leaked video.

Meanwhile, Cyberleek — the person or group responsible for the high-profile GTA 6 leaks that began in the summer — has suggested they will now stop leaking the game. They also claim they will not risk releasing an alleged 200GB build of GTA 6 because their memecoin failed to hit the $30 million market cap target that had been set for its release.

However, Cyberleek claims to have a "dead man's switch" for story spoilers, which they have reportedly threatened to flip if they are threatened, presumably by either Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Yesterday, we reported on how GTA 6 fans were celebrating the crash of the Cyberleek memecoin after the leaker had tied various types of gameplay leaks to its market cap, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. The leaker also threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap.

Earlier this week, a number of gameplay clips were reportedly leaked after market cap goals were hit, including gameplay that allegedly shows Lucia fully naked, and, more recently, the alleged leak of a “Lucia closeup 4k” video.

Cyberleek then threatened to release a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets were met, and launched yet another gameplay poll designed to encourage spending on the memecoin.

However, the Cyberleek memecoin crashed, with a current market cap of $1.2 million, down from a high of $7.8 million on October 11. With those targets now pretty much impossible, it sounds like Cyberleek's crypto scheme has come to an end.

In a new message reportedly posted to their website, Cyberleek declared "the end of the road." In the post, Cyberleek defended their actions from crypto scam allegations, and said Take-Two was "punished enough." "The ending stays unpublished," Cyberleek allegedly insisted in the message. They claimed that while the latest leak does show clips from the final missions of the game, out of context they do not spoil the story.

It's fair to say many fans have taken issue with that suggestion, and are already taking steps to avoid spoilers online.

Cyberleek's message also suggests that the build of GTA 6 they allegedly have access to will not be released because the $30 million market cap was not reached. Cyberleek had said they were raising funds for some mystery project, although many didn't believe the claim. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk," they said, "worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project." They said the memecoin should have been considered a "donation," not an "investment," and hit out at "influencers" who claimed otherwise.

Then, the upshot: "The leeks stop here. For now."

Of course, Cyberleek may release further gameplay and continue with their crypto scheme anyway. They may even release the build they allegedly have. For now though, the more pressing concern is avoiding spoilers sparked by today's leaked video.

Fans had spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and is likely to do so again ahead of GTA 6’s official release date, if they haven’t already. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.

Earlier this week, IGN reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggests access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to nudity in any way, which suggests this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats and won’t be possible in the official release.

One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that reportedly showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.

It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. Recent developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.

In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is Surprisingly More Different Than You Think | IGN Preview
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is far from a 1:1 remake. When I played it, I found familiar rooms containing redesigned challenges that change how the world and player function. I spoke to old friends who had new things to say that added texture to Hyrule and its people. And, I unpacked how its updated controls and detailed art design redefine its old-school combat and puzzle solving for the modern day. This remake isn’t about scope; it’s about depth. The Zelda series is full of old stories, and the Ocarina of Time remake presents itself as a legend retold, with clear theatrical inspirations that have completely changed how I’m approaching it. Previewed by Logan Plant
articles.body:
This is not a 1:1 remake: Expanded dialogue, revamped puzzles, and a detailed new art style prioritize adding depth.

Some structural changes convey a more logically constructed world.

Hyrule is a stage: The remake embraces a theatrical style, which reminds me of one of Ocarina’s original inspirations.

Taking my first steps out of Link’s treehouse and into Kokiri Forest, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake came to life. Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma described this as a “faithful interpretation” of the Nintendo 64 original , and that term stuck with me as I explored Hyrule for more than an hour. This is far from a 1:1 remake: I found familiar rooms containing redesigned challenges that change how the world and player function. I spoke to old friends who had new things to say that added texture to Hyrule and its people. And, I unpacked how its updated controls and detailed art design redefine its old-school combat and puzzle solving for the modern day. This remake isn’t about scope; it’s about depth. The Zelda series is full of old stories, and the Ocarina of Time remake presents itself as a legend retold, with clear theatrical inspirations that have completely changed how I’m approaching it.

First, a quick word about spoilers. I know some of you have never played the N64 game, meaning Ocarina of Time will be a wholly new experience. So, I’m only going to talk about explicitly what I saw in the three chunks I played during the preview. Two sections were split across the first 90-ish minutes of the adventure, while the third and largest section was set in the first dungeon you play as Adult Link, which happens at roughly the one-third mark of the story. So, there will be no spoilers for anything outside of what Nintendo chose to show us.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots

Back to Kokiri Forest. Not counting last-gen upgrades or spinoffs, this is the series’ proper Nintendo Switch 2 debut, and the leap forward in quality immediately drew me in. Rays of light poke through the trees; moss and mushrooms thrive on the withered bark; our hero’s tunic is decorated with handwoven flourishes – and it’s all running at a crisp 60 fps. A pleasant musical performance recreates the forest’s original MIDI theme with what sounds like just a handful of real musicians. Hyrule has never felt more intimately realized than this.

That applies to the dialogue as well. Later, a Castle Town citizen gawks at Link’s outfit, treating him as some foreign outsider from the distant forest: “Intricate stitching that implies the whole ensemble is handmade!” he excitedly says. The forest’s shopkeeper apologizes to Link for his empty shelves, blaming the stubborn Kokiri ringleader Mido for blocking the path to the Great Deku Tree, where the staff goes to restock.

No matter how hard I try to juke Mido, he won’t let anyone pass without a sword and a shield. Here, the remake shows its willingness to change up Ocarina’s level design. After crawling to the secret area that contains the Kokiri Sword, I find that the challenge to reach it has been overhauled. The treasure chest used to be tucked away in the back corner of a maze with a giant boulder – now it’s perched on a high platform in the center of the room, with the boulder rolling around it. The fact that it’s different is interesting on its own, but the way this change impacts what this room is now asking of you reveals a lot.

On N64, this obstacle was about learning to recenter the camera behind Link by tapping Z to see around corners and avoid the boulder. It was teaching you how to play one of the first 3D action-adventure games ever made. This remake no longer carries that burden, and that lesson is unnecessary since the right stick provides complete camera control. Instead, since Link can now jump at the press of a button, this room marks the first time you are required to jump in order to reach the treasure. It stripped out an obsolete tutorial and replaced it with a newly relevant one. My hour in Ocarina was stuffed with nuanced differences like this.

I’m fully equipped now that I have the sword and shield, and Link feels excellent to control. His movement felt immediately familiar to Link in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, with a dash, a jump, and snappy third-person gyro aiming with projectile-based weapons like the slingshot. I was running, leaping, and sniping spiders like a pro in the first dungeon, Inside the Great Deku Tree.

I worked my way to the area I was most looking forward to seeing. Ever since Aonuma’s gameplay demonstration, I’ve been interested in Ocarina’s apparent fascination with a more logically constructed world . As seen in one room of Inside the Great Deku Tree, a floating platform from the N64 game has been replaced by a crumbling bridge that’s now actually built into the environment. I came in with the idea that the remake cares about explaining every element of its world, and my preview session only reinforced that theory.

I was on the lookout for more instances of this in the Forest Temple. Atmospheric fog blankets the ground in this old, haunted mansion where Adult Link hunts down four ghosts. After two open-world 3D Zeldas that largely took a break from the franchise’s traditional dungeons, it felt great to push blocks around, navigate through twisted hallways, and collect small keys. I was reminded of how classic Zelda design welcomes different types of logic and reasoning than Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom’s open-ended approach.

While the Forest Temple’s overall layout was mostly unchanged, it included new cutscenes that fleshed out the dungeon’s antagonists, and yet again showed differences in how specific moments played out. An arena where Link fights a Stalfos used to have a giant hole in the middle. Link needed to avoid it or risk falling to the floor below, but the Stalfos could defy gravity and hover over the gap. You could explain it away as part of this dungeon’s supernatural trickery, but it always looked out of place to me.

Here, that hole has been exchanged for a shallow pool of acid. The skeleton enemies can still walk in it – they don’t have any flesh to lose – while Link takes damage if he enters it. This means the fight plays out the same as it used to: the Stalfos has access to the whole room while Link is constrained to its edges, but the way it’s constructed is more logical. And, when two Stalfos arrive as reinforcements after Link takes out the first, they used to bring a platform with them that filled the room. Now, they just spawn from the acid, making for a more challenging miniboss that forces you to contend with this constraint the whole time.

The fights against the Stalfos were my best look at combat so far. Sword slashes land with a crunchy THWAP, like a loud, powerful, backhanded slap with a striking burst of light to match. Enemy attacks clang off Link’s shield and send him stumbling backwards before his final spin attack sends the Stalfos exploding into a pile of bones. These battles play out with elegant choreography.

Elegant choreography. Atmospheric fog. Handwoven flourishes. Ever since my preview event, I find my mind returning to this anecdote told in an Iwata Asks interview ahead of the release of Ocarina of Time 3D in 2011: On a hot summer day during the development of Zelda for Nintendo 64, designers Toru Osawa, Yoshiaki Koizumi, and Jin Ikeda needed some inspiration. They’d been struggling to figure out how to make swordplay work in a 3D space. Where should the camera focus? How can the player take on multiple enemies at once without getting overwhelmed? These questions spurred a field trip to Toei Kyoto Studio Park, a theme park attached to Toei’s film studios where visitors can see theatrical period drama shows, often featuring samurai.

The heat caused them to duck into a playhouse to cool off. Inside, they watched a stage show where one samurai was fending off a number of ninjas. They noticed that, in this battle, the samurai locked eyes with one enemy at a time. They circled each other as if linked by an invisible tether (or in some cases, literally linked by a chain-sickle), and fought while the others waited their turn to step in. This observation, among others, helped to spark the development of Ocarina of Time’s foundational lock-on Z-targeting system.

I bring this up because it’s clear that live theater inspired Ocarina’s original developers in at least this one key way. As I played the remake of their work, I often felt like I was experiencing Ocarina through the lens of a theatrical period drama at a playhouse.

Take combat, for example: locking onto an enemy narrows the lighting of the scene, putting dramatic emphasis on that invisible tether linking you and your foe. Link weaves back and forth in a dancelike motion, as enemies you aren’t targeting hoot and holler in the background. They, too, are waiting for their turn to strike.

Opening a chest to reap your rewards places an overhead spotlight on whatever treasure you’ve just obtained. Similarly, Floormasters – the iconic disembodied hand enemies that stalk Link from the ceiling – are now telegraphed by a bright spotlight that shines on Link and changes color just before the hand swoops down. These lighting cues feel intentionally theatrical.

The more I thought about this framing on my flight home and in the days that followed, the more I realized just how many design choices fit this theme in some way. Fog covering the ground adds atmosphere as if from a haze machine; Link’s meticulously detailed costume attempts to ground us in the era like it’s a piece of historical fiction; logically constructed puzzles add a practical, handmade feeling to the set; that small handful of musicians could be performing live as the pit orchestra tucked right underneath the stage.

Quest logs are written in past tense, telling an old story: “There once was a young boy named Link who lived in a woodland known as Kokiri Forest.” Even the first reveal trailer opened with a narrator reflecting on ancient events: “Long ago, there was a land called Hyrule…” Ocarina of Time is a play: Hyrule, its stage; dungeons and villages, its sets; enemies and townsfolk, its actors; and Link, its chosen hero.

When I spoke to that Castle Town villager who was stunned to see a boy from the far-off Kokiri Forest, I couldn’t help but think about how sprinting across Hyrule Field to get between the two towns takes less than 90 seconds. A few Peahat enemies dot the landscape, a crack in the ground is begging for a well-placed bomb, but so far, this space that once felt grand and open feels small and quaint in a modern context.

Narratively, characters act like the kingdom of Hyrule is enormous, when practically, it’s very small. Rather than reimagining this version of Hyrule by making it as large as we remember it to be, it reframes each area as a fictional representation of a world much larger than what we actually see. If you’re watching The Wizard of Oz on stage, you understand the yellow brick road to be way bigger than the set shows us. This wouldn’t necessarily excuse any shortcomings that could be found in a Hyrule Field that ends up feeling lackluster by today’s standards – it’s far too early to judge that based on the few minutes I spent with it – but it’s one way to think about how Nintendo altered the meaning of these areas without radically changing their scope.

I was surprised when Aonuma said the team chose to keep the loading screens between areas, but when viewed through this context, it makes a lot of sense: Kokiri Forest, Hyrule Field, and Castle Town are different sets, and the loading screens between them represent the crew swapping them out before the next scene begins. There’s only so much room on the stage.

All of this positions the Ocarina of Time remake as an affectionate retelling of a legend: it is old, it is important, and it is worth revisiting. The storytellers feel there are still things we can learn from it. After seeing just a couple of classic towns and dungeons reborn in this inspired way, I fully agree.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

And, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview.

Logan Plant is IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and DB, and the host of Nintendo Voice Chat. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero.
